Bird migration patterns

Every autumn, millions of birds migrate thousands of kilometers to warmer regions. Arctic terns hold the record, traveling nearly 70,000 kilometers round trip between the Arctic and Antarctic each year.

Many species navigate using the Earth's magnetic field, the position of the sun, and star patterns at night.

Climate change is shifting migration timing, sometimes causing a mismatch between arrival and peak food availability.
